citations.anchor: names the plugin whose onPluginInit throws, and rejects
citations.why: Boots the real createServer with a plugin whose onPluginInit throws and asserts both that the promise rejects with the original error and that Logger.error was called with a string containing the plugin name.

citations.anchor: refuses a body over the configured cap with 413
citations.why: Boots with bodyLimit '20kb' and asserts a 30 kB login body is answered 413 by the parser rather than reaching the credential check, which would answer 401.

citations.anchor: accepts a body well past express’s inherited 100 k
citations.why: A 300 kB body reaches the controller (401, not 413), which fails the moment the cap is inherited from express.json()'s 100 kB default instead of set explicitly.

citations.anchor: is mounted, and describes the prefixed routes, with docs enabled
citations.why: Pins the 'after the prefix' clause only: the generated document's paths contain '/api/auth/login', which is false if setupApiDocs runs before setGlobalPrefix. The 'after the pipe' and 'before listen' clauses are not asserted anywhere.

citations.anchor: sits outside every guard, as an unauthenticated request proves
citations.why: GET /reference/json unauthenticated returns 200 in the same app where GET /api/auth/me returns 401 — pins the 'outside the guards' clause.

citations.anchor: await request(harness.server).get('/reference').expect(200);
citations.why: The routes answer at '/reference', not '/api/reference', on an app carrying the 'api' global prefix — pins the 'outside the global prefix' clause. The 'outside the ValidationPipe' clause is unpinned.

citations.anchor: registers the JSON route first, so it wins a path collision
citations.why: Configures path and jsonPath to the identical value and asserts the response is application/json, which only holds while the JSON handler is registered on the adapter before the Scalar UI.

citations.anchor: returns null, and mounts nothing, when docs are disabled
citations.why: Asserts setupApiDocs(..., { enabled: false }) returns null and that both /reference and /reference/json 404.

citations.anchor: is not mounted with docs disabled (the production default)
citations.why: Both routes are asserted 404 under one flag and both 200 in the sibling enabled case — pins that the JSON is unreachable exactly when the UI is.

citations.anchor: logs the plugin and still serves both the API and the reference
citations.why: A plugin whose docs.decorate throws is logged by name while /reference/json still returns 200 and /api/auth/me still answers — pins 'does not block the start'. The clause about the other plugins' contributions surviving is only implied by the 200, not asserted on the document's content.

citations.anchor: leaves an unknown API path as a JSON 404
citations.why: With staticDir mounted, GET /api/not-a-real-endpoint with Accept: text/html is a 404 whose body does not contain the index page — pins the global-prefix clause.

citations.anchor: does not swallow a non-GET request
citations.why: POST to a client-side route with Accept: text/html is a 404 — pins the non-GET/HEAD clause.

citations.anchor: 404s a missing asset even when the client accepts HTML
citations.why: GET /assets/deleted-chunk.js with Accept: text/html is a 404 — pins the file-extension clause independently of the Accept header.

citations.anchor: gives a JSON client a 404 it can parse, not a page
citations.why: A client-side route requested with Accept: application/json is a 404 — pins the 'does not accept HTML' clause. The /reference clause of this invariant is not exercised: no test mounts staticDir with docs enabled.

citations.anchor: serves the API only, without failing boot, when the bundle is absent
citations.why: createServer resolves with staticDir pointing at a nonexistent folder, the API still answers, and Logger.warn was called with 'No admin bundle at'.

citations.anchor: installs shutdown listeners so in-flight requests are not dropped
citations.why: Asserts the process SIGTERM listener count rises across a real createServer boot, which fails if enableShutdownHooks is dropped. The 'drains rather than tears connections' half is not asserted (the dossier records it as measured by hand).

citations.anchor: expect(process.listenerCount('SIGTERM')).toBe(before);
citations.why: Closes the value createServer returned and asserts the SIGTERM listeners went away, which only works if the return value is the application itself rather than void.

citations.anchor: passes each plugin its own folder and tracking table
citations.why: The fixture supplies `dir: () => '/a/b'` and the assertion is that drizzle received migrationsFolder '/a/b' — so the thunk is invoked at migration time and its result used. The 'never at load time' half is not asserted.

citations.anchor: gives every migration-shipping plugin its own tracking table
citations.why: Takes every shipped plugin carrying migrations and asserts the set of tracking tables is duplicate-free (and all prefixed __drizzle_migrations_), which is exactly 'plugin histories never intersect'.

citations.anchor: applies plugins in exactly the order the host listed them
citations.why: Asserts the sequence of migrationsTable values handed to drizzle equals the host's array order, skipping plugins without migrations.

citations.anchor: names the plugin, how far it got, and the order it depends on
citations.why: A mid-list failure rejects with a message naming the plugin and 'applied 2 of 4 plugin(s)'; the sibling test asserts later plugins are not attempted and nothing is rolled back, i.e. no transaction spans two plugins.

citations.anchor: is idempotent — running it again does not double anything
citations.why: Pins the 'a second run does not double the items' clause: wireSlotContributions run three times over the same contributions leaves one item. The 'before the first render, in one call' clause is a property of createAdmin and is not asserted.

citations.anchor: does not let a consumer mutate the slot through the returned array
citations.why: Pushes, sorts and truncates the array getItems() returned and asserts a fresh getItems() is unchanged — the copy is the assertion.

citations.anchor: redirects a signed-out user from / to the sign-in page
citations.why: Pins the public-route clause: a signed-out visitor is redirected to /identity/signin and that page renders, which is impossible if the public routes were mounted under the pathless layout parent that carries the gate. The 'exactly one pathless parent carrying the first layout found' clause is not asserted against the host.

citations.anchor: shows a recoverable card instead of blanking the app
citations.why: A route chunk that fails to load throws inside the router; the boundary renders its card and #root keeps children — so the boundary is above BrowserRouter.

citations.anchor: a broken page does not take the toast host with it
citations.why: With the crash card showing, Sonner's Notifications region is still attached — pins that Toaster sits outside the boundary.

citations.anchor: the live region is mounted, and empty, before anything happens
citations.why: Asserts the announcer is attached with aria-live=polite and has empty text after the landing page has rendered — both halves of the invariant.

citations.anchor: a second navigation names the new page, not the one just left
citations.why: Pins the 'only a changed heading is announced' clause: arriving at Workspaces behind a Suspense skeleton must not re-announce the outgoing 'Members' heading. The 5-second give-up-silently clause is not asserted.

bootstrap:I-01.reason: The operative clause — 'adding a capability never requires editing a file in packages/bootstrap' — is a claim about future changes, which no harness can evaluate. The 'no guards/tables/routes/screens' half is a judgment about what the source means rather than an observable behaviour; the closest mechanical proxy (a grep for decorators) would pass on a host that had grown domain logic under a different shape.

bootstrap:I-12.reason: tagByResource is module-private in packages/bootstrap/server/src/lib/utils/setup-api-docs.ts:64 and its only input is SwaggerModule.createDocument's output, which emits no path-level `parameters`/`$ref` today; a plugin's decorate runs after tagging, so nothing can inject such a key. The dossier's own testing checklist says the same ('no reachable reproduction'). Reaching the branch would require exporting the function purely to test it.
